title: Treasury-controlled national collection
documented_fact: Parliamentary debate on the Angerstein purchase records that general control and superintendence would lie with the Lords of the Treasury.
why_it_matters: This is contemporaneous evidence that public funding and Treasury authority were present at the Gallery's origin.
limit_or_continuity: Later trustee/director arrangements changed the distribution of authority.

title: Directorate and revised governance
documented_fact: Hansard records the Treasury Minute of 27 March 1855 creating a Director and specifying relations among Director, trustees, Treasury and parliamentary reporting.
why_it_matters: This lets SIDONIE reconstruct an actual change in decision rights rather than relying on a later institutional summary.
limit_or_continuity: The Gallery remained publicly funded and subject to parliamentary Supply.

title: Modern statutory settlement
documented_fact: The Museums and Galleries Act 1992 establishes the current Board/functions and Tate cross-appointment.
why_it_matters: The modern governance architecture becomes statutory rather than resting only on Treasury administrative arrangements.
limit_or_continuity: Public sponsorship remains upstream of the institution.

title: Current sponsor framework
documented_fact: The framework specifies present DCMS accountability, appointments and financial controls.
why_it_matters: It reveals the modern administrative layer superimposed on the statutory Board.
limit_or_continuity: The framework does not replace the 1992 Act.
